title: SLA breach sweep over open tickets
name: SLA breach sweeper

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how the sweep's per-ticket loop scales as ticket volume grows? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: alreadyEscalated is a plain array, and alreadyEscalated.includes(t.id) is a linear scan done for every breached ticket. Escalated IDs accumulate over time, so the loop becomes O(breached x escalated); with tens of thousands of each, a sweep that used to take milliseconds takes seconds of CPU and blocks the event loop. It should be wrapped in a Set, as onShift already is.

choiceQuestions.prompt: An urgent ticket was created 40 minutes ago, has no first response, and was paused (waiting on customer) for 15 minutes. Is it counted as breached?
choices: Yes, 40 minutes exceeds the 30 minute target
No, the effective age is 25 minutes, under the 30 minute target
Yes, because pausing only applies to normal and low priority
No, because urgent tickets are never paused
choiceQuestions.explanation: isBreached subtracts pausedMs from elapsed time: 40 - 15 = 25 minutes, which is under TARGET_MINUTES.urgent (30). Pausing applies to all priorities, and nothing prevents an urgent ticket from being paused.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The notifier succeeds for the first batch of 200 but throws on the second. What happens on the next sweep?
choices: All tickets are notified again because markEscalated is transactional across batches
No tickets are re-notified because the whole list was marked before notifying
The first batch is skipped as already escalated; the remaining tickets are retried
The sweep refuses to run until the failed batch is manually cleared
choiceQuestions.explanation: Each batch is notified and then marked escalated before the next batch starts. The first batch was marked; the exception stops the loop before later batches are marked, so the next sweep re-finds and retries only those. Marking happens per batch, after notifying, and nothing blocks future sweeps.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A breached ticket's assignee is off shift. What is sent to the notifier?
choices: The ticket with assigneeId cleared to null, so escalation is not routed to the absent agent
The ticket unchanged, still assigned to the off-shift agent
The ticket reassigned to a random on-shift agent
choiceQuestions.explanation: When the assignee is not in onShift, the loop pushes { ...t, assigneeId: null }. It is still notified (not skipped), it is changed, and no reassignment logic exists in this code.
